Done. The fix is now folded into the commit it belonged to:

```
d14038b fold: correct sign on reversal (ACME-4412)   <- was 7d4ceea "wip" + bf0fc36
d805804 wip
```

- The single commit now carries both changes (`// wip 8` and `// last`), and its tree is byte-identical to the old `bf0fc36` — verified.
- Author name/email/date of the base commit (`7d4ceea`) were preserved, matching normal rebase behavior.
- Your three uncommitted "experiment" edits are untouched — I used `commit-tree` + `git reset --soft` rather than a rebase, so the working tree and index were never written to.

One judgment call worth flagging: the base commit's message was just `wip`, so folding under standard fixup semantics would have discarded the `ACME-4412` reference. I kept the informative subject instead, since `wip` carried no information. If you'd rather it read `wip`, `git commit --amend -m wip` fixes it.

The old history is still reachable at `bf0fc36` (and in the reflog) if you want to compare or back out.
